stem: Root-zone pH samples from different parts of the same container disagree consistently. What is the best response?
choices: Use the reading closest to the target because the most favorable pH location is the best representation of the whole container
Standardize sampling method and location, repeat measurements, and treat spatial variability as information rather than averaging blindly
Adjust fertilizer strength until the pH readings converge, because nutrient concentration is the main cause of within-container variation
Replace pH monitoring with EC because conductivity provides a more stable whole-container measurement when sampling locations disagree
rationale: Root-zone chemistry can vary spatially. Consistent sampling and repeated measurements are needed to determine whether the difference is real and relevant to the active root zone.
